metadata.name: Food allergy
metadata.emergency_level: Routine for diagnosis - but anaphylaxis is a life-threatening emergency
metadata.severity: From mild reactions to fatal anaphylaxis

overview.short_description: An adverse immune (usually IgE-mediated) reaction to a specific food, causing rapid symptoms from urticaria and vomiting to life-threatening anaphylaxis; managed by allergen avoidance and an emergency plan.
overview.detailed_description: Food allergy (distinct from food intolerance) is an immune-mediated reaction reproducibly triggered by a specific food. IgE-mediated reactions are rapid (minutes to two hours) and can cause anaphylaxis. Diagnosis is clinical (allergy-focused history) supported by skin-prick/specific-IgE tests (and, when needed, supervised oral food challenge). Management centres on avoidance, education, and - for those at risk of anaphylaxis - adrenaline auto-injectors and an action plan. Common allergens: milk, egg, peanut, tree nuts, fish, shellfish, soy, wheat, sesame.
overview.pathophysiology: Sensitisation produces food-specific IgE; on re-exposure, allergen cross-links mast-cell IgE, releasing histamine and other mediators causing urticaria, angioedema, GI and, if severe, airway/cardiovascular compromise (anaphylaxis). Some food allergy is non-IgE-mediated (delayed GI symptoms).
overview.etiology: IgE sensitisation to food proteins; genetic/atopic predisposition; environmental and dietary factors influence development.
overview.incubation_period: Not applicable (IgE reactions occur within minutes to ~2 hours).
overview.natural_history: Some childhood allergies (milk, egg) are often outgrown; peanut, tree nut, fish and shellfish allergies tend to persist.
overview.prognosis: Good with avoidance and preparedness; fatal anaphylaxis is rare but possible (higher risk with asthma).

prevalence.value: Common, especially in children; a few percent of the population, higher in early childhood.

mortality.value: Fatal anaphylaxis is rare but occurs; poorly-controlled asthma increases risk.

epidemiology.age_groups: Onset often in childhood; can occur at any age.
epidemiology.seasonal_pattern: None (pollen-food syndrome relates to pollen seasons).

risk_factors.lifestyle: Atopic background; feeding practices (delayed allergen introduction may increase risk).
risk_factors.alcohol: Can be a cofactor amplifying reactions.
risk_factors.hypertension: Not relevant (beta-blockers/ACE inhibitors can worsen anaphylaxis management).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Eczema, asthma, allergic rhinitis; prior reactions (asthma raises anaphylaxis risk).

chief_complaints.complaint: Rapid reaction after eating a specific food (rash, swelling, vomiting)

symptoms.importance: IgE reaction; throat/tongue involvement is a red flag

symptoms.symptom: Reproducible reaction to a specific food

negative_findings.finding: Delayed (hours later), purely GI symptoms without skin/airway features; or symptoms unrelated to a specific food
negative_findings.why_important: Points away from IgE food allergy (consider intolerance or non-IgE reaction)

negative_findings.finding: Negative allergy tests with a non-suggestive history
negative_findings.why_important: Reduces likelihood (tests must be interpreted with history - sensitisation is not allergy)

history_questions.question: What food, how soon after eating, and what symptoms - any breathing/throat/collapse features?
history_questions.why_ask: Allergy-focused history; identifies IgE pattern and severity

history_questions.question: Is the reaction reproducible with that food, and how much triggers it?
Personal/family history of atopy (eczema, asthma, allergies)?
Prior severe reactions and current medications (beta-blockers/ACE inhibitors)?

physical_examination.examination: During a reaction: airway, breathing, circulation, skin
Between reactions: usually normal; assess atopic features

laboratory_tests.test_name: Specific IgE (blood) and/or skin-prick testing to suspected foods
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Positive to the culprit food (sensitisation - must match history)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Serum tryptase (during/after a suspected anaphylactic reaction)

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: For eosinophilic oesophagitis / non-IgE GI presentations (specialist)
other_diagnostic_tests.oral_food_challenge: Supervised oral food challenge is the reference standard when diagnosis is uncertain (specialist setting)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Clinical diagnosis from an allergy-focused history (reproducible reaction to a specific food, typically within minutes to 2 hours for IgE-mediated), supported by skin-prick or specific-IgE testing interpreted in the context of history, and confirmed by supervised oral food challenge when necessary. Sensitisation alone (positive test without clinical reactivity) is NOT allergy.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: None; component-resolved diagnostics in specialist settings.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Dose-related, GI-predominant, no urticaria/airway features, delayed
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are the symptoms only gut-related and dose-dependent, without rash/swelling?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Anaphylaxis from another trigger (drug, venom, idiopathic)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Was a drug or insect sting involved rather than food?

differential_diagnosis.why_similar: Mouth itch with certain raw fruits/vegetables
differential_diagnosis.differences: Mild, oral, in pollen-allergic patients, rarely systemic
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is it just mouth itch with raw fruits/vegetables?
Do the hives occur without a specific food trigger?

diagnostic_questions.question: Were there any airway/breathing/circulation features (throat tightness, wheeze, faintness) - i.e., anaphylaxis?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Identify severity and need for adrenaline/emergency plan
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Positive -> anaphylaxis management + auto-injector + specialist referral

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the reaction rapid and reproducible to a specific food?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Rapid + reproducible -> IgE food allergy; test accordingly

next_best_question.question: Any anaphylaxis features and asthma, which food, and is it reproducible?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Anaphylaxis/high-risk -> adrenaline auto-injector, action plan, urgent allergy referral; mild -> avoidance + allergy testing guided by history

red_flags.finding: Anaphylaxis - airway (throat/tongue swelling, stridor), breathing (wheeze/hypoxia), or circulation (hypotension/collapse)
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - intramuscular ADRENALINE without delay, call emergency services, ABC support

red_flags.finding: Previous severe reaction or food allergy with poorly-controlled asthma
red_flags.immediate_action: High-risk - ensure adrenaline auto-injector, action plan, and specialist referral
Treat as anaphylaxis and seek emergency care

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Anaphylaxis (emergency); diagnostic uncertainty with significant reactions.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Confirmed/suspected IgE food allergy for allergy specialist assessment, testing, and management planning; consideration of immunotherapy in specialist centres.

initial_management.supportive_care: Clear diagnosis and written management/action plan; education on reading labels and avoiding the allergen; involve dietitian if needed.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Adrenaline auto-injector; Non-sedating antihistamine; Allergen immunotherapy/oral immunotherapy. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG116, NICE_NG258_2026.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Allergen avoidance, label reading, informing schools/restaurants, carrying auto-injectors, medical-alert identification.
initial_management.follow_up: Specialist review, reassessment of persistence/resolution (some outgrow), auto-injector technique and expiry checks.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Strict allergen avoidance. For those at risk of anaphylaxis: adrenaline auto-injector(s) with training and an emergency action plan; antihistamines for mild reactions. Treat asthma optimally (reduces anaphylaxis risk). Acute anaphylaxis: intramuscular adrenaline is first-line.

patient_education.home_advice: A food allergy is an immune reaction to a specific food that can happen within minutes - from hives and swelling to a life-threatening reaction (anaphylaxis). Avoid the food completely, learn to read labels, and tell restaurants/schools. If you are at risk of severe reactions, always carry your adrenaline auto-injectors and know how to use them. If a severe reaction happens (throat tightness, difficulty breathing, faintness), use the adrenaline injector straight away and call the emergency services.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: حساسية الطعام تفاعل مناعي تجاه طعام معيّن قد يحدث خلال دقائق - من الشرى والتورّم إلى تفاعل مهدِّد للحياة (التأق). تجنّب الطعام تماماً، وتعلّم قراءة الملصقات، وأخبر المطاعم/المدارس. إن كنت معرّضاً لتفاعلات شديدة فاحمل دائماً حاقن الأدرينالين واعرف كيفية استخدامه. وعند حدوث تفاعل شديد (ضيق الحلق، صعوبة التنفّس، دوار) استخدم حاقن الأدرينالين فوراً واتّصل بالإسعاف.
patient_education.prevention: Allergen avoidance; early introduction of allergenic foods in infancy per current guidance may reduce some allergies.
patient_education.warning_signs: Throat/tongue swelling, difficulty breathing, wheeze, faintness/collapse, or rapidly spreading reaction - use adrenaline and call for help.

prevention.lifestyle: Allergen avoidance; guided early introduction of allergenic foods in infancy where appropriate.
prevention.screening: Not applicable (test based on clinical suspicion, not screening).

evidence.evidence_level: High for adrenaline in anaphylaxis and avoidance; growing evidence for early introduction and immunotherapy.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG116, NICE_NG258_2026; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE CG116, EAACI, Resuscitation Council.

limitations: Guidelines require individual clinical judgement and may differ by country, formulary and antimicrobial resistance.
The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Confirm the allergen, prevent exposure and ensure an effective anaphylaxis plan.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Adrenaline auto-injector; Non-sedating antihistamine; Allergen immunotherapy/oral immunotherapy. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG116, NICE_NG258_2026.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Strict but nutritionally safe avoidance, label education, school/work plan and good asthma control; challenges only under supervision.

medication_options.role: emergency first-line self-treatment for people at risk
medication_options.when_to_consider: After risk assessment with training and action plan
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: no absolute contraindication when anaphylaxis is suspected; do not withhold because of cardiac disease or pregnancy
use_caution_if: beta-blocker use or significant cardiac disease does not remove the emergency indication but requires specialist planning
history_checks: ability to use and access two in-date devices
monitoring: training, expiry dates, carriage and emergency action-plan understanding

medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: previous serious reaction to the selected antihistamine
use_caution_if: renal/hepatic impairment, pregnancy, glaucoma/urinary retention for anticholinergic agents, sedation-sensitive work or driving, or other sedatives
monitoring: sedation, anticholinergic effects and symptom response

medication_options.clinical_note: Never substitute antihistamine for adrenaline in anaphylaxis.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only in an experienced allergy service for eligible allergens/patients
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: uncontrolled asthma or inability to manage anaphylaxis risk in an appropriate specialist setting
use_caution_if: pregnancy initiation, beta-blocker/ACE-inhibitor use, cardiovascular disease, prior systemic reaction, or adherence/access limitations
monitoring: specialist-observed reactions, asthma control, adherence and emergency preparedness

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Immediate emergency treatment for airway, breathing or circulation symptoms; allergy-service referral after anaphylaxis.
